technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the reactor-based processor as a Spring XD module with a minimal processor-class option and extensible module options for additional configuration.
Use Reactor 2.0 RC1 APIs and update Maven dependency management and affected integration points consistently rather than maintaining compatibility with earlier Reactor APIs.

Implement the Redis field-value counter aggregation as an incrementally updated Redis-backed module, using atomic Redis operations and configurable key and field-value mapping where supported by the existing module conventions.
Treat the duplicated U3 and U4 requirements as one Redis aggregation feature and do not implement it twice.
Implement the RxJava processor as a separate processor module using the existing Spring XD processor lifecycle and message conversion conventions.
Expose the HTTP source maximum message size through servers.yml while preserving the existing 1 MB default when no override is supplied.
Move Hadoop-specific tests and their supporting test dependencies into a separate project while preserving test behavior and preventing Hadoop dependencies from affecting DIRT classpath generation.
Implement XD plus YARN acceptance tests as infrastructure-driven tests that deploy a minimal representative XD flow on YARN and validate successful message processing.
Use the repository's existing build, testing, configuration, Redis, deployment, and documentation conventions wherever possible.
assumptions: The work targets an existing Spring XD codebase with established module APIs, Maven builds, test utilities, documentation structure, and deployment scripts.

The referenced previous field-value-counter specification is available to the developer through repository history, archived documentation, or equivalent project artifacts; effort includes reconciling it with the current codebase.
Redis is already an accepted runtime dependency and a test Redis instance or embedded/test-container equivalent can be used for automated tests.
The Reactor 2.0 RC1 dependency and compatible transitive dependencies are available from configured repositories.
The RxJava version and APIs can be selected consistently with the existing project dependency policy; no long-term backward compatibility layer is required.
EC2 and YARN credentials, images, network access, and a usable test environment are available; provisioning a new cloud account or redesigning the deployment platform is outside scope.
Acceptance tests need to cover a representative simple XD feature on YARN, not every module or failure mode.
Documentation updates include module reference documentation, configuration examples, defaults, and operational limitations, but not a full user guide rewrite.
Normal implementation, unit testing, integration testing, build troubleshooting, and developer-level validation are included; independent QA staffing and elapsed waiting time are excluded.
The estimate represents one developer's direct work-hours and excludes calendar delays caused by external reviews, infrastructure provisioning, or unavailable dependencies.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module model, Reactor and RxJava integrations, Redis abstractions, HTTP source adapter, Hadoop test layout, YARN deployment support, build configuration, and historical field-value-counter behavior. Convert the user stories into implementation and test tasks.

Upgrade dependency management to Reactor 2.0 RC1, resolve API and transitive dependency changes, update affected production and test code, and verify the full build against Java 17-compatible project requirements.

Design and implement the minimal reactor processor module contract, including processor-class declaration, lifecycle integration, message input/output handling, error behavior, and factory or registration metadata required by Spring XD.

activities.activity_name: Reactor module options, tests, and documentation
activities.activity_description: Add well-known module option commands or equivalent configuration metadata for additional reactor processor settings. Create unit and integration tests for minimal and configured processors and document configuration examples and defaults.

Port the prior aggregation specification into the current module architecture, implement continuous field-value counter updates in Redis using atomic operations, define key and value handling, integrate module configuration, and handle invalid or unsupported input according to project conventions.

Identify gaps between the historical specification and current requirements, add unit and Redis-backed integration tests for accumulation, multiple fields, restart behavior, and edge cases, then update reference documentation and examples.

Implement the RxJava-based processor module, including RxJava API integration, conversion between Spring XD messages and RxJava streams, processor lifecycle and error handling, module metadata, and representative processing examples.
Add unit and integration coverage for normal processing, stream completion, errors, and configuration. Document the RxJava processor's usage, supported configuration, and limitations.

Expose the HttpChunkAggregator maximum content size through servers.yml, preserve the 1 MB default, validate configuration values, wire the setting into adapter creation, and add focused tests for defaults, overrides, and oversized messages.

Create or adapt a separate project for Hadoop-specific tests, move test sources and resources, adjust dependency and build configuration, remove unnecessary Hadoop dependencies from DIRT, and verify correct Eclipse classpath generation and test execution.

activities.activity_name: XD plus YARN on EC2 acceptance tests
activities.activity_description: Define a minimal end-to-end scenario, implement deployment and setup automation for XD on YARN in EC2, add acceptance test orchestration and assertions for message processing, and implement cleanup and failure diagnostics.

activities.activity_name: Build, CI, and cross-feature integration stabilization
activities.activity_description: Run the complete unit, integration, acceptance, and packaging test suites; resolve cross-feature dependency and configuration issues; validate clean builds and generated artifacts; and integrate the acceptance path into the build cycle.

Consolidate reference documentation for the new processor modules, Redis aggregation, HTTP configuration, and operational test prerequisites; update examples and release notes; and perform final packaging and implementation review.
